newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - A$1 bln agreement boosts Australia gas reform.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - A$1 bln agreement boosts Australia gas reform.

text.p: The A$1 billion settlement between the Victorian state government and Bass Strait oil and gas producers over a long-running tax dispute removes a major obstacle to reform of Australia's gas industry.
Analysts said the settlement also paves the way for the expected sale of Victoria's gas transmission and distribution businesses and several gas-fired power stations.
Under the agreement, the Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd will share a lump-sum payment of about A$1 billion with joint-venture partner Esso Australia Resources Ltd, a subsidiary of Exxon Corp.
BHP said it would receive A$511 million, for an after tax profit of about A$167 million, while the settlement opened the way for it to sell Bass Strait gas interstate.
BHP's share price jumped sharply on the news, closing up A$0.55 at A$18.15, its highest close since late June.
The dispute centred on a petroleum resource rent tax, which was imposed by the federal government on Bass Strait gas production from July 1990.
At issue was whether BHP and Esso had the right to pass on the tax under its existing contracts with Victorian government-owned entities GasCor and Generation Victoria.

Victoria's auditor-general recently noted the state had a nominal exposure of $A3 billion, with a net present value of $A1.9 billion, if BHP and Esso were successful in passing on the cost of the tax.

Analysts said the main benefit to BHP lay in the boost the decision gave to gas market reform, which is being pursued by the Council of Australian Governments to develop an open and competitive gas market.
BHP could look to sell gas in New South Wales, Australia's most populous state, while it would also be able to sell gas directly to customers in Victoria.
BHP external affairs group manager Robert Porter told Reuters: "We see the greatest market demand for gas in NSW, given the fact that gas penetration in NSW is significantly lower than in Victoria."
"Gas prices in NSW are also higher than they are in Victoria so we think there is a market we can capture in NSW."
Analysts said gas accounts for about 17 percent of the energy market in Victoria, but only about eight percent in NSW, where the Australian Gas Light Co has been the sole distributor.
BHP is a partner in a proposed A$380 million pipeline to supply Bass Strait gas to NSW along the east coast of Australia.
The sale of Victoria's gas transmission and distribution businesses, meanwhile, has been widely expected.
A spokesman for Victorian treasurer Alan Stockdale said in July that any privatisation remained on hold until settlement of the tax dispute.
The government owns the gas pipeline network, Gas Transmission Corporation, and the gas utility GasCor, along with the 500MW Newport and 450MW Jeeralang gas-fired power stations.
GasCor was expected to be broken up and sold in a number of distribution regions, a Sydney-based energy analyst said.
Potential buyers could include AGL, which made its interest known earlier this year, and Victoria's privatised electricity distributors. -- Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
